The Summer Witch, Founder of the Jul'library, Adept of the Witches Gathering — House Miser / Vellanet Rise, The Witches Gathering, The Jul'library, Independent Scriptorium

Status: Active — resident scholar and wandering conjurer at Vellanet Rise; founder of the Jul'library; affiliated with the Witches Gathering; maintaining spatial boundary wards across the Midlands margins

July Summer Miser is the second of the five Miser children—born alongside Jack and Archie in the triplet threshold of High Summer—and the arcane anchor of the household. While Jack took to the sword and the Silver Flame's rigid muster roll to feed the cottage, and Archie was consumed by unstable third-eyed pyromancy, July mastered the disciplined geometry of the School of Conjuration. She founded the Jul'library—a roaming repository and scriptorium of bound spaces and extraplanar compendiums based out of Vellanet Rise—and maintains close ties with the Witches Gathering, a loose fellowship of Midlands hedge-scholars and planar herbalists. Patient, sharp-eyed, and carrying the household's emotional weight beneath a tall pointed witch's hat, she commands spatial transposition with clinical precision and keeps an owl familiar named Barnaby watching the tree lines.

Status: Active — enforcing Section 14 Cordon property mandates inside the Overgrown Manor despite ongoing planar collapse

Quartermaster Cornburary is the Iron Legion logistics and supply officer attached to the Colour Division detachments operating near the Midlands border. Completely immune to supernatural terror, atmospheric dread, and rampant plant monsters, Cornburary evaluates military operations exclusively through ledger balances, equipment wear, and authorized property requisitions. When sent to enforce Hjumpik's overdue Aegis Magi contract, he treated the collapsing, briar-choked Feywild manor not as a magical crisis, but as an unauthorized structural alteration with an itemized depreciation fee.

The King Who Held the Door — Koopa Troop (King) / Disaster Inc. (current situation)

Status: Active — operating in the Shadow Estate; carrying necromantic evidence; royal war chest active; illegal under hostile mandates and still completely unbothered

Bowser is the King of the Koopa Troop, a giant fire-breathing turtle-dragon who was cast into the Shadowfell during the Planar Fracture alongside Archie Miser. Since then, he has attended a vampire dinner party where he presumably sat wherever he wanted, tackled a vampire lord through a gothic window, bit a giant bat's wing, and most recently held a door shut against an axe-wielding succession claimant while Markop was unconscious—then punched said claimant in the head and picked up a necromancer's wand asking 'Is this a magic wand?' with the innocent curiosity of a child finding a toy. Waluigi has arm-wrestled Bowser and LOST. Waluigi has also competed against Bowser in every sport imaginable. Bowser is not complicated. Bowser is EFFECTIVE. The current party pass identifies Bowser as Disaster Inc.'s blunt-force sovereign: door-holder, threat magnet, and walking siege engine whose honesty remains more reliable than most alliances.

Evidence

  • Claws — “Bowser is a giant turtle who breathes fire, wants things, and takes them.”
  • Bowser's Shell Bash — “When Orangus Cornelius threatened to turn Bowser's shell into a soup bowl, diplomacy ended because YOU DO NOT THREATEN BOWSER'S SHELL.”
  • Fire Breath (Recharge 5–6) — “Bowser is a giant turtle who breathes fire, wants things, and takes them.”
  • Extra Attack — “Bowser operates on simple logic: see problem, hit problem, problem either stops being a problem or gets hit again.”
  • The Shell — “When Orangus Cornelius threatened to turn Bowser's shell into a soup bowl, diplomacy ended because YOU DO NOT THREATEN BOWSER'S SHELL.”
  • Indestructible — “Bowser is the most INDESTRUCTIBLE.”
  • Kidnapper of Princesses — “Bowser is traditionally an ANTAGONIST—kidnapping princesses, conquering kingdoms, generally being the obstacle that heroes overcome.”
  • King of the Koopas — “- Koopa sovereignty: every alliance with Bowser is also a negotiation with a kingdom.”

The Quartermaster Spy Who Itemized The Apocalypse — Mages' Guild

Status: Active — operating with the Mages' Guild, recently ear-dragged, still tracking receipts somehow

Thornbury is a stuffy, penny-pinching Mages' Guild operative who charged Archie 2,000 gold for a broken rope. He later brought Archie and Bones rubber duckies for a bubble bath, only to be dragged away by the ear by a disgruntled noblewoman. He left behind a notebook proving he was spying on the party the entire time. Waluigi has zero respect for a spy who is defeated by a bath time interruption. Thornbury is the Mages' Guild operative who proves that evil does not always arrive with a death ray, a monologue, or even decent posture. Sometimes evil arrives with a ledger, a rope, and a reimbursement policy. He accompanied Agent L, Luigi, and Archie through the ruined manor while secretly gathering intelligence on the party, cataloguing environmental anomalies, pocketing suspicious rings, uncovering hidden stashes, and charging Archie 2,062 gold pieces and 5 silver for breaking a single rope. He is a field spy, quartermaster, scavenger, emergency supplier, expense auditor, and apparently a man who believes no supernatural catastrophe is too urgent for itemized billing. He brought practical supplies to dangerous situations, helped navigate the manor, provided rope, potions, a Sending scroll, and a tensor box, and then managed to undermine all professional credibility by getting caught taking a heated luxury bath while soldiers suffered outside. Byscilla Danos dragged him away by the ear like an embarrassing child, and in his haste he left behind field notes proving he had been spying on everyone the entire time. Waluigi despises nearly everything about Thornbury on principle. Unfortunately, historical accuracy requires admitting that the man is actually COMPETENT, which is infuriating. WAH.

Evidence

  • Itemized Dagger — “In another room, Thornbury pocketed a ring from the floor.”
  • Guild Hand Crossbow — “Thornbury is a stuffy, penny-pinching Mages' Guild operative who charged Archie 2,000 gold for a broken rope.”
  • The Itemized Invoice (2,062 GP) — “The bill totaled 2,062 gold pieces and 5 silver.”
  • Quartermaster's Field Pack — “His field pack was notably well-stocked: - Adventurer's basics: bedroll, mess kit, tinderbox, torches, rations, waterskin - Healer's kit with multiple uses remaining - Two potions of healing - One potion of invisibility”
  • Tensor Box Detection — “He deployed a tensor box—an arcane detection device that Archie did not understand, which is not surprising because Archie understands fire and very little else consistently.”
  • Surveillance Journal — “Byscilla Danos dragged him away by the ear like an embarrassing child, and in his haste he left behind field notes proving he had been spying on everyone the entire time.”
  • Rubber Ducky Bath Contingency — “He later brought Archie and Bones rubber duckies for a bubble bath, only to be dragged away by the ear by a disgruntled noblewoman.”

Even in haunted ruins or active warzones, Thornbury reserves generator-heated water and rubber duckies for personal maintenance. If compromised or caught by superiors (such as Byscilla Danos), he can grovel to disengage freely and slip away into shadows.

His field pack was notably well-stocked: - Adventurer's basics: bedroll, mess kit, tinderbox, torches, rations, waterskin - Healer's kit with multiple uses remaining - Two potions of healing - One potion of invisibility
He deployed a tensor box—an arcane detection device that Archie did not understand, which is not surprising because Archie understands fire and very little else consistently.
Byscilla Danos dragged him away by the ear like an embarrassing child, and in his haste he left behind field notes proving he had been spying on everyone the entire time.
He later brought Archie and Bones rubber duckies for a bubble bath, only to be dragged away by the ear by a disgruntled noblewoman.

The Reluctant Ghostbuster — Mushroom Kingdom / Mages' Guild (Contractor)

Status: Active — recovered alive from Bowser's lava-moat tunnels, treated at Dr. Toad's Star Hill Clinic, and under a two-week rest order; Mario remains absent.; as of 2 Aethel, 1035 BF reported — unverified — to be in the clinic's 'private wing, high security, consciousness fluxing', while something wearing his clothes stood outside in three copies

Luigi is the reluctant ghostbuster, the brother left behind by every heroic story that needed Mario in front, and the man whose history now carries the unresolved shadow of Mr. L, Guild contracts, haunted technology, medical testimony, and a disappearance mystery too large to fit inside the word sidekick. Waluigi finds Luigi infuriating, sympathetic, suspicious, brave, evasive, and extremely bad at choosing restful employment. The Poltergust is not just a vacuum; it is Luigi's proof that fear can be weaponized into duty. The Garden Above the Fire confirms that Luigi survived the lava-falls aftermath, recalled the line 'The star is not lost. Find the garden above the fire,' and reached Dr. Toad's clinic alive — still wounded, still asking for Mario, but no longer missing in the compound tunnels.

The Plumber Who Vanished — Mushroom Kingdom (Former Hero) / Unknown

Status: Missing — Presumed alive, location unknown, last confirmed sighting 1039 BF at the Star Fountain

Mario is—or WAS—the most famous hero in the Mushroom Kingdom. The man who saved Princess Peach countless times before her assassination in 955 BF. The red-capped plumber who could jump higher than physics should allow, who stomped Bowser's schemes into the ground repeatedly, who was so synonymous with heroism that his NAME became a verb. And then, after eighty-five years of diminished appearances and growing silence, he DISAPPEARED entirely. Luigi found him at the Star Fountain. They flew together on wing caps. Luigi said 'Nothing can hurt us... as long as we're together.' And then Mario was GONE again, and Luigi is working alone for the Mages' Guild at Raventree Manor, sucking up ghosts with a vacuum cleaner and refusing to explain ANYTHING. Waluigi has spent considerable effort piecing together what happened. The picture that emerges is worse than a simple disappearance. WAH. The Garden Above the Fire does not return Mario; it makes his absence louder, because Luigi's rescue ends with Luigi asking the brother who is not in the room whether they are still superstars.

Mario cannot willingly abandon an innocent in danger he can see. He has advantage on saving throws against effects that would make him flee or stand aside.
